chunks: From him, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jabalah, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥārith, from Bakkār, from Muḥammad ibn Shurayḥ, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the time of Maghrib, and he said: “When the redness in the horizon changes, and the yellowness goes away, and before the stars become intermingled.”

key_terms.الصُّفْرَةُ: the yellowish light that disappears as evening sets in
key_terms.الْأُفُقِ: the horizon where the sunset signs are observed
key_terms.الْحُمْرَةُ: the redness visible in the horizon at sunset
key_terms.تَشْتَبِكَ النُّجُومُ: the stars appearing densely and intermingled in the sky
key_terms.وَقْتِ الْمَغْرِبِ: the appointed time of Maghrib salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: When does the time of Maghrib salat (prayer) begin according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal indication for identifying the time of Maghrib salat (prayer) by visible changes in the horizon. It describes the onset of Maghrib through the changing of the redness, the disappearance of yellowness, and before the stars become densely visible.
